blocks.text: The relative atomic mass of chlorine is 35.5. No single chlorine atom weighs 35.5 units — you cannot have half a nucleon. The number is an average, and understanding why unlocks one of the most reliably examined calculations in WAEC Chemistry.

blocks.markdown:
## Inside the atom

An atom has a tiny, dense **nucleus** containing protons and neutrons, surrounded by electrons moving in shells. Almost all the mass sits in the nucleus; almost all the volume is empty space where the electrons move.

blocks.title: Atomic number and mass number
blocks.text: The atomic number Z is the number of protons in the nucleus and it defines the element. The mass number A is the total number of protons and neutrons, also called nucleons. Therefore number of neutrons = A - Z. In a neutral atom the number of electrons equals the number of protons.

blocks.markdown:
### Notation

An atom is written with the mass number above and the atomic number below the symbol. For sodium with A = 23 and Z = 11:

- protons = 11
- neutrons = 23 - 11 = 12
- electrons = 11 (neutral atom)

### Ions

An **ion** is a charged atom. It has gained or lost electrons, but the nucleus is untouched, so the proton and neutron counts never change.

- Na+ has lost one electron: 11 protons, 10 electrons
- O2- has gained two electrons: 8 protons, 10 electrons

blocks.title: The commonest error in this topic
blocks.text: Forming an ion never changes the number of protons or neutrons. If a question tells you an ion has a 2+ charge, subtract two from the electron count only. Changing the proton count would change the element itself.

blocks.markdown:
## Isotopes

**Isotopes** are atoms of the same element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. They therefore have the same atomic number but different mass numbers.

Because chemical behaviour depends on electron arrangement, and isotopes have identical electron arrangements, **isotopes have identical chemical properties**. They differ only in physical properties that depend on mass, such as density and rate of diffusion.

Common examples: chlorine-35 and chlorine-37; carbon-12, carbon-13 and carbon-14; hydrogen-1, hydrogen-2 (deuterium) and hydrogen-3 (tritium).

blocks.title: Relative atomic mass from isotopic abundance
blocks.prompt: Chlorine consists of 75 percent chlorine-35 and 25 percent chlorine-37. Calculate its relative atomic mass.

steps.text: Relative atomic mass is the weighted average of the isotopic masses, using the percentage abundances as weights.
Work out each product: 35 x 75 = 2625 and 37 x 25 = 925.
Sanity check: the answer must lie between 35 and 37, and closer to 35 because chlorine-35 is the more abundant isotope. It does.

blocks.answer: The relative atomic mass of chlorine is 35.5

blocks.title: Check your average
blocks.text: A weighted average must always fall between the smallest and the largest isotopic mass, and must lean towards the more abundant isotope. If your answer falls outside that range you have divided by the wrong number, which is usually a sign that the abundances were given as fractions rather than percentages.

points: Protons and neutrons occupy the nucleus; electrons occupy shells around it.
Atomic number is the proton count and identifies the element; mass number is protons plus neutrons.
Neutrons = mass number minus atomic number, and a neutral atom has equal protons and electrons.
Forming an ion changes only the electron count, never the protons or neutrons.
Isotopes have the same proton number but different neutron numbers, so they share chemical properties.
Relative atomic mass is the weighted average of isotopic masses across natural abundance.
